subject: Benchmarking playbook + requested evidence pack for TelcoSys RFP
messages:
From: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@telcosys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: TelcoSys Procurement <procurement@telcosys.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: TelcoSys RFP - performance evidence request

Diego,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. TelcoSys is consolidating vendor performance evidence for our cloud inference platform RFP. Attached is a short spreadsheet with the metrics we need (latency envelopes by prompt type, concurrency scaling, cold/warm start characteristics, and a short list of test harness constraints). Can you confirm Redwood can provide a reproducible runbook and the raw artifacts (CSV/JSON) used to produce the charts?

Key asks:
- p50/p95/p99 latency under 3 concurrent traffic shapes: baseline (3Q mix), burst (90th percentile spike), and steady high QPS.
- throughput vs concurrency curves with model variant and quantization noted.
- warm vs cold start penalty and how KV cache behavior was controlled.
- reproducible load driver (open-source harness or script) and exact simulator config.

We have a procurement deadline of Oct 14. If you can supply a runbook + evidence pack by Oct 6, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — cc'd procurement for timeline.

Regards,
Aisha Rao
TelcoSys — Sourcing Manager

Attachment: telcosys_benchmark_spec.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@telcosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TelcoSys RFP - performance evidence request

Aisha —

Thanks for the spec and timeline. Short answer: yes, we can provide a reproducible runbook and the raw artifacts. Below is a concise deliverable plan and a couple of clarifying questions so we ensure apples-to-apples comparability.

Planned deliverables (by Oct 6):
- Redwood runbook (markdown) that documents the exact model variant, quantization flags, runtime kernel choices, sequence lengths, and batching strategy used to produce each chart.
- Raw CSVs (latency samples, per-request metadata, CPU/GPU utilization timeline) + aggregated quantile tables.
- The exact load driver (we'll share a containerized k6 + python harness) and an example config for the three traffic shapes.
- Short README with commands to re-run the baseline experiments and instructions to reproduce KV/cache warmup behavior.

Clarifying questions:
1) For "cold start", do you want an instance cold (process-level cold) or model-cache-cold (KV cache empty but runtime already up)? We can show both but need to know which you prefer for scoring.
2) Which model from our catalog should we use for the primary evidence? You listed an LLM-2 family inference workload in the spec — we can run the 7B quantized variant and include a 13B as a sensitivity case.

Operational notes we will include in the runbook:
- How we measured tail latency (p99 measured with 99.9% confidence intervals using 30-minute steady-state windows).
- How we isolated background noise (dedicated GPUs, disabled noisy processes, pinned IRQs).
- How batching and prefix caching were instrumented and the exact flags used.

I'll attach the first draft runbook and a heatmap of per-token latencies once we run the baseline tomorrow. Marissa/Ben: looping you in for any deal-level constraints (SLA/formatting/legal artifacts).

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v1.md (draft runbook stub)

From: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@telcosys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TelcoSys RFP - performance evidence request

Diego —

Thanks, that plan looks good. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- For scoring we will treat "model-cache-cold" (KV cache empty) as the primary cold-start metric, but please include the process-level cold numbers in an appendix.
- Primary target model: please use the 7B quantized variant as the baseline. Include the 13B sensitivity test but mark it as "informational".
- Please include the exact OpenTelemetry/metrics keys you emit for latency and GPU utilization — we will map those into our scoring pipeline.

One small ask: can you provide a short note on how batching affects p95 vs p99 in your experiments? If you can include two runs (no-batching vs adaptive batching), that would be ideal.

We appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the artifacts.

Regards,
Aisha

Attachment: none

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rao <aisha.rao@telcosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:23:00 -0700
Subject: Deliverables: runbook, raw artifacts, and re-run instructions (TelcoSys)

Aisha —

Attached is the evidence pack per your spec. Summary of contents and quick notes:

Evidence pack (attached):
- redwood_runbook_v1.md — step-by-step commands, environment variables, and kernel/quantization flags.
- latency_heatmap_q3.csv — raw sample-level per-token latency for the baseline run.
- throughput_vs_concurrency.csv — aggregated throughput samples across concurrency sweep (1–128).
- harness_config_baseline.json — the exact k6 + python harness config we used.

Highlights and synthetic summary:
- Baseline (7B quantized, no batching): p50=18ms, p95=54ms, p99=98ms at 20 QPS steady (single-replica).
- Burst scenario (90th percentile shaped spike, adaptive batching enabled): tail increases ~1.6x at p99 relative to steady baseline; batching reduced CPU/GPU overhead and improved end-to-end throughput by ~22% but added median tail pressure on p95 under certain mix distributions. The runbook includes the adaptive batching thresholds.
- Cold-start (KV empty): additional median penalty of ~120ms and p99 penalty of ~310ms versus warm baseline; process-level cold start (container cold) showed higher penalties as expected and is in appendix.

Operational artifacts we included: exact OTel metric keys (redwood.latency_ms, redwood.gpu_util_pct, redwood.batch_size), the docker image digest used for the runtime, and the scripts to produce the visualizations.

Next steps:
- If you want we can containerize the entire harness and push a reproducible image to your test account.
- Marissa/Ben: marking this as deliverable complete for the RFP. Can you confirm any additional procurement paperwork?

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency_heatmap_q3.csv (CSV stub), throughput_vs_concurrency.csv (CSV stub), harness_config_baseline.json (config stub)
